subject: Commit increase: hosted API capacity and soft-throttle schedule
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@fastparcel.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commit increase: hosted API capacity and soft-throttle schedule

Elena —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. As discussed, FastParcel is seeing consistent month-over-month growth and you'd like a predictable hosted commit rather than relying on ad-hoc bursts. Attached is a cleaned up proposal with two paths: a 12-month committed uplift (Option A) and a 6-month stepped ramp (Option B). Key points: 

- Proposed baseline commit: 15M tokens / month (current: 6M)
- Burst pocket: +30% monthly for peak windows (tested for Black Friday cadence)
- Soft-throttle policy: gradual token throttling during sustained 95th-percentile utilization spikes; customer-visible warnings + automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model where needed
- Billing cadence: monthly invoice with usage reconciliation against commit at month end

Can you confirm if procurement will need a PO or formal SOW to start? I've also cc'd Laura (onboarding) to confirm rollout timeline and required ops artifacts.

Next steps I propose: you confirm preferred path (Option A or B), procurement contact confirms PO terms, Redwood generates SOW and a 30-day implementation window is scheduled with Ops.

Attachments: FP_commit_proposal_v2.pdf (PDF, 310KB)

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0186

--
Redwood Inference — Production-grade LLM inference for engineering teams
From: Elena Rossi <elena@fastparcel.com>

Cc: Jake Mullins <procure@fastparcel.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:45:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Commit increase: hosted API capacity and soft-throttle schedule

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the proposal and the clear options. A few questions before I take this to procurement: 

1) SLA and latency: can you confirm the P99 latency targets for our account at the 15M commit level? We need to include that in the procurement packet.
2) What is the guaranteed burst behavior? Is the +30% an absolute guarantee or best-effort?
3) Can you clarify the invoicing currency and whether we can be billed quarterly instead of monthly (finance asks).

Procurement (cc'ed) will confirm whether they need a SOW or PO template. I am leaning to Option B (6-month stepped ramp) because it aligns with our internal forecasting but would like your ops team's input on the rollout window.

Also please include any security/compliance attestations we should attach to the procurement packet (SOC2 report link or standard data handling summary).

Best,
Elena Rossi
VP Product, FastParcel
elena@fastparcel.com

Subject: Re: Commit increase: hosted API capacity and soft-throttle schedule

Elena —

Thanks for the quick review. Short answers below and I added Karthik (our infra/product ops lead) to confirm rollout and latency expectations.

1) SLA / latency: For the 15M commit on our Dedicated-hosted profile, we target P50 < 50ms, P95 < 220ms, P99 < 420ms under normal operational load. We'll include the exact targets and disclaimers in the SOW.
2) Burst behavior: The +30% burst pocket is a guaranteed buffer for scheduled peaks (up to a pre-negotiated monthly cap). For sustained overages beyond the burst pocket we use soft-throttle with customer-visible notifications; emergency ad-hoc increases can be added with 48h notice in most regions.
3) Billing cadence: We can offer quarterly invoicing for enterprise customers — I'll flag this with finance and include billing terms in the SOW.

Security artifacts: I'll attach our SOC 2 Type II summary and a data handling one-pager in the SOW packet.

Next: if Option B is preferred, we propose this ramp:
- Month 1: 9M commit baseline (allow 20% burst)
- Month 2–3: 12M commit baseline (allow 25% burst)
- Month 4+: 15M commit baseline (allow 30% burst)

I've attached the SOW draft for procurement review. Laura — can you confirm a realistic ops start date if procurement signs within 7 business days?

Attachments: SOW-draft-FastParcel.docx (DOCX, 120KB)

Thanks,
Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 11:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit increase: hosted API capacity and soft-throttle schedule

Ben / Laura —

Quick ops readout for FastParcel's Option B ramp: 

- Capacity: 15M tokens/month at steady-state is well within our hosted pool for the us-west region; will reserve a soft pool for scheduled peak windows.
- Rollout timeline: 30 calendar days from signed SOW to initial configuration (DNS, API keys rotation window, quota mapping). For stepped ramp we'll do two configuration pushes (start + month 3) — minimal downtime, rolling changes.
- Throttle policy: Recommend the following customer-visible thresholds: 80% warn, 95% soft-throttle (10–20% rate reduce with advisory header), 110% deactivate burst and fall back to compatible model. We'll provide a webhook for utilization alerts to your monitoring and a per-route token breakdown in the console.
- Ops artifacts: putting together ops-rollout-checklist.xlsx and a short runbook for your SREs.

I also confirmed the P99 latency numbers Ben quoted in staging and we see those medians in internal tests; production will vary by model selection — we recommend pinning model versions for the first 60 days to reduce variance.

Links:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/FP-2027-09-U1
- Draft runbook (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/drive-fp-runbook

I'll loop in Platform if we need to schedule a dry-run.

-Karthik
Senior Product Ops, Redwood Inference
